newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Cabinets given mauling by the press - for charity.
newsitem.headline: Cabinets given mauling by the press - for charity.

text.p: The European Commission was licking its wounds on Monday, a day after its various cabinets were given a severe mauling by the press.
But it was all in the name of charity, as the Media Mob -- a motley collection of journalists covering the European Union -- managed to win the Commission's inter-cabinet football tournament.

The Media Mob -- probably inspired by a two-year tradition which dictates that the losing finalists have to organise the next year's event -- prevailed 2-1 in a best-of-three penalty shootout after a scoreless final.
The event -- which raised nearly 500,000 francs for reconstruction in Bosnia -- was organised by Regional Policy Commissioner Monika Wulf-Mathies, whose cabinet were runners-up.
Some 24 teams took part in the six-a-side tournament. All had to feature at least three cabinet members and one woman.
Commissioner Neil Kinnock was the pick of the senior officials playing -- proving as adept in goal as he is at defending his transport policy.

Franz Fischler, the farm commissioner, was "mooed" every time he went near the ball, although his team entered into the spirit by wearing T-shirts bedecked with a mad cow -- the subject that has preoccupied his officials for much of this year.
